newsitem.title: INDIA: India SEBI permits all firms to list on OTCEI.
newsitem.headline: India SEBI permits all firms to list on OTCEI.

text.p: Indian market regulator, the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), said on Monday that it had decided to permit all companies to trade on the Over the Counter Exchange of India (OTCEI).
SEBI Chairman D. R. Mehta told a news conference that the 250-million-rupee cap on firms registering on OTCEI had been lifted.
SEBI said in a statement that it had decided to accept some of the recommendations of the Dave panel of experts on OTCEI trading.

One of these was: "SEBI should remove the upper limit of Rs 25 crores and allow all companies, irrespective of the size, to list on the OTCEI, on the same lines as the other stock exchanges," the statement said.
The equity shares of all unlisted companies would be allowed to be traded on the OTCEI, the statement said.

SEBI also accepted a recommendation by the Dave panel that companies with no record of having paid dividends in three successive years of the previous five and have not been appraised by financial institutions be allowed to raise funds by listing on OTCEI.

But these companies have to fulfill two conditions -- they must be sponsored by an OTCEI member and must appoint at least two market makers to provide continuous liquidity to the stock, the market regulator said.

"OTCEI was an exchange with beautiful features but was not performing. We appointed a committee which gave these recommendations, which hopefully would be reviving OTCEI," Mehta told Reuters after the news conference.
SEBI also amended a regulation for custodians which requires them to have a minimum net worth of 500 million rupees.
Some custodians had urged SEBI to relax the net worth norm, Mehta said.
"The board considered the request and decided to allow these custodians to increase their net worth to 500 million rupees in a phased manner over a period of 5 years," he said.
Mehta said the government would soon approve a stock lending scheme.
"The stock lending scheme is likely to be declared by the government of India shortly," he said.
